titleEn: Even in the Dark, Dad Is Here!

pages.text: "Dad, don't put out the lamp!" Little brother Mumu called from the covers, with only his big head showing. Beyond the round window was a dark, snowy night. Dad from the mill stopped reaching a wing toward the little lamp.
"When it goes out, I hear creaking. I want to sleep with it on." Mumu disliked darkness most of all. Under the next covers, big sister Dodo was already asleep.
"Sleep well." Dad blew out the lamp. The room was all dark! Then, outside the window, creak... creeeak... Mumu pulled the covers up to his beak and trembled.
"Sob... Dad..." Hearing the little cry, Dad came quietly upstairs with a lamp. "You were scared. It's okay." He sat beside the covers and held Mumu's wing tight.
Dad leaned toward him. "Can you tell me what scared you?" Mumu pointed at the round window. "There... a creaking monster." Dad nodded. "I understand. Shall we look together?"

Dad opened the window and held out the lamp. Light flashed over the wheel, stopped for the night and rocking in the wind. Creak... creeeak... "Look! The creaking monster was the waterwheel!" Mumu's beak opened by itself.
"What about that rattle?" Mumu pointed a wing, and Dad shone the lamp. "A shutter!" Mumu called. One by one, the light showed nothing scary. Dad patted his back. "Even in the dark, Dad is here."
Mumu didn't tremble now. "Dark just means the lamp is out!" Under the covers, he flicked his tail once.
Dad taught him, "One, say, 'I'm scared!' Two, shine the lamp on things one by one! Three, hold Dad's wing tight!" Mumu held Dad's wingtip in both wings and nodded his big head.
The bedside lamp glowed very softly. Dad laid a broad wing on Mumu's back. "It's okay to be scared. I'm just downstairs." Snuggling beside Dodo, Mumu whispered, "Even in the dark, Dad is here!"
